description:
FILED s473d (Opus, 2026-09-07) while fixing #1248(c) (SvREADONLY on an array).
PRE-EXISTING and NOT part of that family: it diverges for an ORDINARY WRITABLE
array too, and reproduces on a git-archive extraction of c4304834.

MINIMAL REPRO (perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl):

    no warnings;
    my @w = (1,2,3);
    print "concat  ", "n=" . @w, "\n";      # perl: n=3     PCL: n=ARRAY(0x1)
    print "concat2 ", @w . "", "\n";        # perl: 3       PCL: ARRAY(0x1)
    print "eq      ", (@w eq "3" ? "y":"n"), "\n";  # perl: y  PCL: n

THE ASYMMETRY IS THE FINDING.  An array in scalar context collapses to its
element count on the NUMERIC side and not on the STRING side:

  * %to-number-raw has `((and (vectorp val) (adjustable-array-p val)) (length val))`,
    so `0+@w` and `@w == 3` are right;
  * stringify-value has `((vectorp v) (format nil "ARRAY(0x~(~X~))" ...))`,
    which treats the array's own storage as if it were a reference, so
    `"" . @w` and `@w eq "3"` are wrong.

`"@w"` (interpolation) is a DIFFERENT path and is correct -- it joins with $".

CANDIDATE FIX AND ITS RISK (measure before writing it).  The symmetric change
is one clause in `stringify-value`, above the `(vectorp v)` reference clause:

    ((and (vectorp v) (not (stringp v)) (adjustable-array-p v))
     (%p-fixnum-string (length v)))

`%pcl-scalar-collapse` already writes exactly that rule for the assignment
path, so this is its string half (CLAUDE.md 11: reuse it rather than a fourth
copy).  THE RISK is the clause it would shadow: today a RAW adjustable vector
reaching `stringify-value` prints as ARRAY(0x...), and the question that must
be answered first is whether any array REFERENCE ever reaches a string slot as
a raw vector rather than as a p-box (references are boxes, so the expected
answer is no, but `stringify-value` is on every print path and the measurement
is cheap: instrument the clause to record its callers over a full sweep).

The alternative layer is the EMISSION -- `.`, `eq` and friends impose scalar
context on their operands, and `%pcl-scalar-collapse` at the operator would be
the general answer -- but `p-.` is a hot path and the runtime clause is free.

NOT scheduled in s473d: that brief is the numeric-representation family, and
this is the string half of a different mechanism.
subject: An array in scalar context collapses to its element count for NUMBERS but not for STRINGS: `"n=" . @a` gives ARRAY(0x1) where perl gives n=3 (writable arrays too)
